newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Phillips wins Venezuela Ambrosio oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Phillips wins Venezuela Ambrosio oil deal.

text.p: U.S. company Phillips Petroleum agreed Wednesday to pay $31.1 million for the contract to operate Venezuela's Ambrosio oil field, state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said.

Only one other company, Enron Oil & Gas bid for the field offering $15.7 million on the third day of Venezuela's third round of oil operating contract auctions. Total bids soared to nearly $1 billion in the first two days.
The offshore Lake Maracaibo field, discovered in 1974, currently produces 3,300 barrels per day (bpd) from 20 active wells. Proven reserves are 114 million barrels, according to PDVSA estimates.

Under the 20-year contract, the operator will produce hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Lagoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale. The operator must also invest at least $27 million within three years, although PDVSA expects total investment to be higher.
A total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts to be sold this week with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids.
